summary: A well-made IELTS listening paper. Parts 2-4 are the right length and have real distractors (corrections, options mentioned and then ruled out). Part 1 is short (about 570 words) and Part 4's notes copied the lecture's words too closely; I reworded three note lines and one box option so students must catch a paraphrase, as in the real test.
strengths: Part 1 has genuine IELTS traps: the receptionist corrects the date (15th -> 22nd) and the time (5.00 -> 5.30), gives last year's price before the current one, and warns about the pharmacy next door.

Part 2 MCQs each mention all three options, with two of them clearly ruled out (fire/housing, grant/land sale, noise/dust/parking); the matching box has used distractors (benches paid for by donations, stalls reserved for village producers, kitchen paid for by a charity).
Part 3 is a good academic discussion; both multi-select pairs work by elimination, with every wrong option discussed and rejected.
Part 4 is a coherent lecture of about 770 words with answers in order and clean one-word gaps.
Parts 2, 3 and 4 are 770-910 words, matching real timing.

issues.problem: Part 1 script is only about 570 words, shorter than a real Part 1 (roughly 650-800 words), so it plays quickly and gives little thinking time between answers.
issues.change: Report only (audio already recorded). If re-recorded, add one more exchange, e.g. the caller asking about parking or a mobile number read out with a correction.

issues.problem: Script inconsistency: Otabek says 'Doctor Karimov suggested traffic flow... we can't pretend it was his idea', but the tutor is 'she' later in the same conversation (Q25). If Karimov is the tutor, the gender flips; if not, option C 'a suggestion made by their tutor' is never directly addressed. The key B is still clearly right.
issues.change: Script not changed (recorded). Corrected the Q21 explain, which said 'The tutor proposed traffic flow', to quote Doctor Karimov. If re-recorded, make the tutor consistent (e.g. 'Doctor Karimova suggested ... her idea').

issues.problem: Box option G 'will not be open until next year' was word for word the script ('it will not be open until next year'), so the answer could be matched without understanding.
issues.change: Option G is now 'is still being completed' (script: 'because it isn't finished'). Explain/evidence updated; key stays G.

issues.problem: Option E 'can be hired for private events' and option B (Q18) 'is open only during the summer' are almost word for word in the script, which makes those matches easier than IELTS.
issues.change: Left as is (they still need the right section). Suggest rewording to e.g. 'is available to rent for celebrations' and 'operates for part of the year only' in a future edit; paraphrase pairs now point to 'weddings, parties, company evenings' and 'from May to September'.

issues.problem: Part 4 notes for Q34, Q38 and Q39 copied the lecturer's words exactly ('because fat absorbs scent', 'began as a town of tanners', 'the first important synthetic scent'), so no paraphrase had to be recognised.
issues.change: Reworded the note lines: 'because fat takes up scent' (which the explain already used), 'was originally a town of leather workers', 'the first major artificial scent'. Answers unchanged.

issues.problem: Several other Part 4 note lines are still very close to the script (Q31 'through {{31}}', Q40 'without picking it'), making Part 4 a little easier than a real lecture task.
issues.change: Suggest paraphrasing more of the note stems in a future edit.

issues.problem: Paraphrase pair used 'medicines', which is the answer itself, not a phrase the student reads in the table.
issues.change: Pair is now ['Could you bring', 'Patient should bring'].

issues.problem: Paraphrase pair ['reminder letters', 'reminder by text'] pointed at the distractor and its question side ('reminder by text') is not in the table.
issues.change: Pair is now ["you'll get a reminder", 'Reminder sent by'].

issues.problem: Paraphrase pair ['reflects everything straight back', 'the height of the nearby buildings'] did not say the same thing.
issues.change: Pair is now ['the buildings on either side', 'the nearby buildings'].

issues.problem: Small script slips (not changed): two consecutive lines by speaker A in Part 1 ('A brush for the gaps. Right.' / 'And what does it cost?'); 'It was you, wasn't it. Your flat.' in Part 3 should end with a question mark.
issues.change: Report only; harmless for the audio.

issues.problem: The paraphrase checker's question-side test is circular: it searches JSON.stringify(q), which contains the vocab pair itself (and explain/evidence), so a wrong inQuestion always passes. Q8, Q10 and reading Q2/Q18/Q25 had broken question sides that the checker accepted.
issues.change: Suggest excluding vocab, explain, evidence and answer from qText in scripts/check-paraphrases.mjs. I verified every pset11 pair separately against the visible prompt/options/note/table/notes/box.
